creativity.reason: Level 0: the filing fully describes the products (financial, tax and marketing software), and none of them creates or enables artistic or storytelling work.

community.reason: Level 2: there is employee development plus specific external activities (Prosperity Hub training in underserved communities, paid volunteering and donation matching), but no participant, dollar or reach figures that would support level 3.

cross_cultural.reason: Level 2: there are specific current practices (ERGs with no membership figures, a hiring program for underserved communities, and language-based advisor matching), all limited in shown reach.

entrepreneurship.reason: Level 4: enabling small businesses and solopreneurs through payments, financing, marketing and start-up accounting tools is a major reported segment at 60% of revenue; level 5 was not chosen because the segment also serves mid-market firms and accountants, and 40% of revenue is consumer tax and personal finance.

evidence.indicators: Segment is 60% of fiscal 2026 total revenue; Intuit overall serves approximately 93 million consumers, businesses and accountants (no separate small-business count)

notes: Mailchimp was considered for Creativity but scored 0, because it is a marketing tool (email, ads, landing pages) rather than creative software, and brand marketing is a listed trap; it is counted under Entrepreneurship only. QuickBooks ProAdvisor training and certification for accountants (also mentioned in the Item 7 excerpt as ProAdvisor Program memberships) was left out of Community as commercial product training. Prosperity Hub is partly a way for Intuit to staff its own support centers, but it also trains people through partner employers in underserved communities, so it is counted once each under Community and Cross-cultural. Equal-opportunity language and the Stronger Together and We Care and Give Back values are general statements and were not scored on their own. A restructuring plan was announced in May 2026; the filing does not say it cut any of the programs above. Neither Community nor Cross-cultural gives any figures, so a sustainability report could add context, though coverage was judged sufficient and no second look is triggered.
